title: NetworkNotificationPushRequest
description: network.notification-push-request@1: bodies of network.notifications.push on OpenVibe.Network (a service token holding the capability). POST /internal/notifications/push: { user_id | subject, type?, title?, message?, … } creates one notification (400 without user_id or subject; 404 for an unknown subject). POST /internal/notifications/push-bulk: { user_ids | subjects, …same fields } creates it for each recipient (400 without a non-empty user_ids or subjects, or with more than 1000). Recipients are Network user ids or canonical usr_ subjects; a subject resolves to its account, so a service that knows the person by subject (Vision's consent request, Cam's event alert) need not hold the numeric id. Unknown fields are ignored; 503 when the notification service is not running. The other /internal/notifications/* routes (unread, mark-read, resolve-users) take the internal key only and are not part of this capability.

user_id.description: A Network user id (already translated from the caller's own ids).

type.description: A notification type from openvibe-shared/notifications (STREAM_LIVE, FOLLOW, MENTION, …); it supplies the default category, priority, icon and title. Stored as GENERIC when absent.

sender_id.description: The actor's Network user id; with no actor_subject, a recipient who blocked this person gets nothing.

service.description: The sending service. A service token may only name its own (svc:live → live); anything else is 403 capability.owner_denied.

priority.description: low, normal, high or critical (openvibe-shared PRIORITY); default the type's, else normal.

category.description: Default: the type's category, else system. A recipient who switched the category off gets nothing; moderation, system and admin notices are never hidden by a block.

rich_content.description: Any JSON value, stored and returned as given.

expires_at.description: When it may be deleted (SQLite datetime, UTC).

actor_subject.description: The actor as a usr_ subject for the block check; null: no known person (no block check).

subject.description: The recipient as a canonical usr_ subject, instead of user_id. It resolves to that person's Network account; an unknown subject is 404 and creates nothing.
